findings.summary: The wrote-flag extraction is fail-open: if the guard's stdout JSON is unparseable the inline node reader (and the `|| echo "false"` fallback) yields "false", so a structurally broken verdict silently passes the guard instead of failing closed. Every other production-bus read path in this entry fails closed (exit 3); this one should too.

A firing guard overwrites LOOP_EXIT unconditionally with 3, clobbering the drain classifications (4 = wall-clock/backstop, 5 = drain failure) set earlier in the loop. The failure is still loud and non-zero as spec §1 requires, but the run's exit code no longer distinguishes which failure came first.

readProdBusRunWriteVerdict re-reads board:agent-runs from channel_seq 0 on every run; at the real production head_seq (~9k per spec §0 GT-P1) that is ~90 sequential paged GETs. The before-run read already knows that channel's head_seq, so the scan could start from it (after_seq) without weakening the identity judgement.

In the GT-P2 entry tests the `res.code !== 0` assertion is not independently discriminating, because LOOP_ENGINE_CLI is deliberately absent so the drain loop already exits non-zero. The real discrimination is carried by the prod_bus_guard_wrote=true / offenders / existingRunChannels assertions, which do go red if the guard is deleted or downgraded.
